ap_calculus_bc-m01.stem: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane. Its horizontal velocity $x'(t)$ for $0\le t\le 8$ is given by the graph shown, which consists of line segments. The particle's $x$-coordinate at $t=0$ is $2$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the particle at $t=8$?

stimulus.description: Graph of x'(t), consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: x(b) = x(0) plus the signed area under the graph of x' from 0 to b (trapezoids, negative below the axis).
Reads x'(8) from the graph as if it were the position x(8).
Uses width 1 instead of width 2 for each trapezoid.
Reports only the signed area and forgets the initial position x(0).

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Recover a position coordinate from the graph of its velocity component
student_thinking: Read the vertices of the graph of x'
Compute signed trapezoid areas from 0 to the upper limit
Add the initial position

key_conditions.condition: x(b)-x(0) equals the integral of x' and x' is piecewise linear

verification.independent_path: signed area from adaptive numerical integration of the piecewise-linear x' (independent of the trapezoid formula)

stimulus.description: Graph of r = f(theta), consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: Omits the factor 1/2 in the polar area formula.
Computes (1/2) times the integral of r instead of r squared.
Area = (1/2) times the integral of r^2 d(theta); on each linear piece the integral of r^2 is (r0^2 + r0 r1 + r1^2)/3.
Squares the integral of r instead of integrating r squared.

Reads a vertex of the graph of r' without checking for a sign change from positive to negative.
Confuses the minimum of the graph of r' with the maximum of r.

ap_calculus_bc-m04.stem: The function $f$ has derivatives of all orders. The graph of $y=f^{(4)}(x)$ on $0\le x\le 4$, consisting of line segments, is shown. Let $P_3$ be the third-degree Maclaurin polynomial for $f$. Which of the following is the Lagrange error bound for $|f(2)-P_3(2)|$ obtained from the graph?

stimulus.description: Graph of f^(4)(x), consisting of line segments connecting the plotted vertices.

options.why: Uses the largest signed value of the graph instead of the largest absolute value.
M a^4 / 4! with M the maximum of |f^(4)| on [0, a], read from the graph.
Divides by 3! instead of 4!.
Uses the power 3 instead of 4 for the x-term.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Read a bound on a derivative from its graph and apply the Lagrange error bound
student_thinking: Read the largest absolute value of f^(4) on [0, a] from the graph

key_conditions.condition: |f^(4)| <= M on [0, a] holds for the graph's maximum absolute value

misconceptions.description: uses a maximum from outside [0, a]

verification.independent_path: maximum absolute value found by dense sampling of the piecewise-linear graph (independent of vertex reading)

ap_calculus_bc-f01.title: Euler's method and a logistic model

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A population $P(t)$ of fish in a lake, in hundreds, at time $t$ years satisfies the logistic differential equation $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=P\left(1-\dfrac{P}{400}\right)$ with $P(0)=20$. Use Euler's method with two steps of equal size, starting at $t=0$, to approximate $P(2)$. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric_rows.criterion: Slope at (0, P(0)) from the differential equation
First Euler step with step size 1 (value)
Second Euler step using the updated value of P (answer)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the Euler's method approximation from part (a) an overestimate or an underestimate of $P(2)$? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: Underestimate: d²P/dt² = P'(1 - 2P/400) is positive while 0 < P < 200, so the solution is concave up and tangent-line steps lie below it.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the reason: shows the solution is concave up using the sign of d^2P/dt^2 = (dP/dt)(1 - 2P/400) while P < 200
Concludes Euler's method gives an underestimate because the tangent lines lie below a concave up solution

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Without solving the differential equation, find $\lim_{t\to\infty}P(t)$ and find the value of $P$ at which the population is growing fastest. Explain your answers.
parts.model_answer: The limit is the carrying capacity 400; growth is fastest at P = 200, the maximum of P(1 - P/400).

rubric_rows.criterion: Limit equals the carrying capacity (value)
Fastest growth at P = 200, justified as the maximizer of P(1 - P/400) (value)
required_elements: maximum of dP/dt as a function of P

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A different population $Q(t)$ satisfies the same differential equation with $Q(0)=480$. Is $Q$ increasing or decreasing at $t=0$? Interpret your answer in the context of the model.
parts.model_answer: dQ/dt = Q(1 - Q/400) < 0 when Q > 400, so Q is decreasing: a population above the carrying capacity declines toward it.

rubric_rows.criterion: Determines the sign of dQ/dt at Q = 480 (negative)
Interprets: above the carrying capacity the population decreases toward the carrying capacity

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_bc
blueprint.concept: Approximate a solution with Euler's method, judge the approximation by concavity, and interpret a logistic model without solving it
student_thinking: Apply Euler's method twice, updating P each step
Use the sign of d2P/dt2 to judge over/underestimate
Read carrying capacity and fastest growth from the logistic equation
Interpret the sign of dP/dt above the carrying capacity

key_conditions.condition: The Euler values stay below 200 and the solution stays in the lower half, so concavity is up on [0,2]
key_conditions.evidence: checked in code with the closed-form logistic solution

verification.independent_path: Euler iteration repeated in floating point and compared with the closed-form logistic solution to decide over/underestimate (independent of the exact-rational generation)
